newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice falls sharply on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice falls sharply on long liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended down sharply in slow trade on Friday on long liquidation, traders said.

The key October contract ended limit-down at 2,085 yuan ($251) per tonne, losing 85 yuan. It opened at 2,085 and stayed at that level for the whole session. December fell 36 yuan to 2,019 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 1,100 tonnes from 2,100.
Traders said investors offset their long positions, which triggered sharp falls today.
"Some investors were eager to sell while few wanted to buy because of poor sentiment," one trader said.
Traders said further drops would be limited after successive falls over the past few days.
"Current prices are far below spot prices and futures are likely to find some support at the 2,000 yuan level in the short term," a second trader said.
The price of spot rice is around 2,400 yuan per tonne.
